title: Taifa of Dénia
capsule: The Taifa of Dénia was founded around 1010 by Mujāhid al-ʿĀmirī, a Slavic (Saqaliba) freedman who had served as a high official of the Caliphate of Córdoba during its disintegration; he established control over the port of Dénia and the Balearic Islands, which his fleet seized in 1015, making the taifa a significant naval power in the western Mediterranean. Mujāhid launched a costly and ultimately failed invasion of Sardinia around 1015–1016, repelled by Pisan and Genoese forces, but the Balearics remained under Deniyan control for decades. After Mujāhid's death his son Iqbāl al-Dawla ruled until the taifa was absorbed by the Almoravid empire; the Balearics submitted to Almoravid authority around 1116. The polity's survival to 1250 in the dataset likely reflects the continued distinct governance of the Balearics before their conquest by James I of Aragon in 1229.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The core political history of the taifa is reasonably attested in Arabic chronicles, but territorial mapping of the maritime domains and their later status is approximate.
